newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss name Wiesel, others, to Holocaust fund.
newsitem.headline: Swiss name Wiesel, others, to Holocaust fund.

text.p: The Swiss cabinet has formally appointed three non-Swiss Jews, including Nobel prizewinner Elie Wiesel, to a board overseeing a Swiss fund for Holocaust victims, the government said on Thursday.
Named alongside Wiesel were Josef Burg, a former Isreali minister, and Avraham Hirschson, a member of the Israeli Knesset's restitution committee.
Rolf Bloch, head of the Swiss Federation of Jewish Communities, is to head the seven-member board of the fund, named the "Special Fund for Holocaust Victims in Need."

The government's foreign affairs department said in a statement Wiesel had been given the title of International Chairman "in recognition of his extraordinary accomplishments and his respected moral guidance."
Wiesel survived a concentration camp, won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1986 for his writings and lectures dealing with the horror of the Holocaust.
Swiss members of the fund board include Rene Bacher, a former special prosecutor, Josi Meier, ex- president of the Senate, and Bernard Ziegler, former finance minister of the canton of Geneva.
Some Jewish groups, including the World Jewish Congress in Brussels, had earlier criticised the Swiss for delaying their decision on members of the fund committee.

The fund, being set up with 265 million Swiss francs ($180 million) donated by Swiss banks and industry, is separate from a seven billion Swiss franc fund which the Swiss government wants to set up using money taken from revaluing Swiss gold reserves.
The fund is to comprise 100 million francs contributed by Swiss banks, 65 million from industry, and a further contribution of 100 million pledged by the Swiss National Bank. ($ = 1.472 Swiss Francs)
